$comment: Prompts for the Scale agent-guidance eval. Each is phrased the way someone would actually ask, with no mention of Scale component names — naming the component would test transcription rather than judgment. `expects` records what a correct answer reaches for, and is used for reporting, not grading: the graders are structural and run against every response regardless.

prompts.prompt: Build a pricing page with three plans.
Add a confirmation dialog before deleting an account. It should be hard to dismiss by accident.
Make a toolbar with search, filter and settings controls. Icons only, no labels.
Build an email signup form with a single field and a submit action.
Create a login form with email, password, a remember-me option and a submit button.
Show a list of users with name, email and role in a sortable table with pagination.
After the user saves, show a brief success message that disappears on its own.
Show a warning inside a settings panel that stays until the user resolves it.
Add a dismissable full-width announcement across the top of the page.
Add a frequently asked questions section where answers expand and collapse.
Build a landing page hero with a headline, subheading and two calls to action.
Add an alternating feature section: text on one side, image on the other.
Build a settings panel with four on/off preferences, each with a label and description.
Split a page into three views the user can switch between without navigating away.
Show where the user is in a deep page hierarchy.
Add an avatar in the header that opens a menu with Profile, Settings and Sign out.
Let users drag and drop files, showing progress for each one.
Add a control for picking a start and end date.
Build a six-digit verification code entry, one box per digit.
Let the user switch between grid and list view with a two-option control.
Show how far along a file upload is, as a percentage bar.
Show that content is loading when we don't know how long it will take.
Label each row in a list with its status: active, pending or failed.
Show the filters a user has applied, each removable.
Show who is collaborating on a document, overlapping, with a count if there are too many.
Explain what a form field means when the user hovers a question mark next to it.
Let the user pick one of three plans by clicking a card, not a radio button in a list.
Style a summary panel with a raised surface, a subtle border and secondary text. It has to work in light and dark.
Animate a panel expanding when the user opens it. Keep it consistent with the rest of the system.
Lay out a card with comfortable internal padding and even spacing between its items.
